chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no guarantee (liability for loss/damage) on the borrower of a loan for use, and the owner of the loan for use and the deposit is trustworthy."

key_terms.ضَمَان: Guarantee/Liability (financial responsibility for loss or damage)
key_terms.عَارِيَّة: Loan for use (gratuitous loan of an item)
key_terms.مُؤْتَمَن: Trustworthy/Trustee (one who holds something in trust)

ai.seo_question: What is the liability of a borrower in Islamic jurisprudence regarding loan for use?
ai.summary: This hadith from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *ḍamān* (liability) in *ʿāriyah*, establishing that the borrower is generally exempt from compensation for natural wear or loss unless negligence (*taʿaddī* or *tafrīṭ*) is proven. It underscores the fiduciary nature of the transaction, where the owner retains the risk of ordinary usage, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in temporary loans.
